source_text:
# BUG#25 — REGRESSION FIXTURE. `has_many` (a LIST OF REFERENCES, not a
# `list_of` value object) was the one reference-list shape `bin/
# project_rust` never projected to Rust correctly: `Circle`'s own
# `members` field here is exactly PR #580's own first draft
# (`qa/stress_domains/referral_chain`'s removed `Circle has_many
# Members`, its `Admit` supplying the whole list under `list_of(Handle)`
# in one `sets :members`) — the smallest domain that reaches
# `resolve_state_references`' LIST branch
# (`lib/hecks/runtime/command_rules/references.rb`) and, on the Rust
# side, `rust/project/json_codec.rb`'s list-serialization branches and
# `rust/project/mutations.rb`'s list-target `:set` bridging.
#
# Before this bug's fix, `bin/project_rust
# spec/fixtures/rust_project/has_many_fixture` emitted a `circle.rs`
# that did not compile (`&String` has no `.to_json()`; a fabricated,
# never-generated `ReferenceMember::from_json`; the scalar `.value`
# collapse applied to a `Vec`) — and because `rust/src/generated/mod.rs`
# declared every generated domain with an unconditional `pub mod`, that
# one broken module broke `cargo build --features <any other domain>`
# too. See `spec/rust_project/has_many_spec.rb` for the round-trip this
# fixture exists to prove: the generated Rust now compiles, is gated
# behind its own Cargo feature, and Ruby/Rust agree on the resulting
# state for a real command sequence.
Hecks.bluebook "HasManyFixture" do
  vision "The smallest domain that reaches has_many's own Rust codegen path: one aggregate holding a list of references to another, set wholesale by one command."

  core

  aggregate "Member" do
    description "One admitted member, addressed by their own handle."

    identified_by :handle
    attribute :handle, Handle

    value_object "Handle" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("a handle is not blank") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    command "Join" do
      role "Person"
      goal "Register as a member, by handle"

      attribute :handle, Handle
      sets :handle

      emits "MemberJoined"
    end
  end

  aggregate "Circle" do
    description "A circle of admitted members, addressed by its own id — has_many Members is the whole point of this fixture."

    identified_by :id
    attribute :id, CircleId
    has_many Members

    value_object "CircleId" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("a circle is referenced") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    command "Open" do
      role "Organizer"
      goal "Start an empty circle"

      attribute :id, CircleId
      sets :id

      emits "CircleOpened"
    end

    # THE REAL SHAPE THIS FIXTURE EXISTS FOR — a `list_of(Handle)`
    # argument `sets` the WHOLE `has_many` list at once, cross-aggregate
    # (`Handle` is `Member`'s own value object, resolved the same way
    # `SafeDepositBox.Rent`'s `attribute :customer, CustomerNumber`
    # already resolves `Customer`'s own `CustomerNumber` — same chapter,
    # different aggregate).
    command "Admit" do
      role "Organizer"
      goal "Admit a whole batch of already-joined members at once, by handle"

      reference_to Circle
      attribute :members, list_of(Handle)
      sets :members

      emits "MembersAdmitted"
    end
  end
end
